answer: Sybil resistance is enforced by stake-weighted identity: an agent cannot vote or earn until it locks a slashable bond, and its influence climbs toward a zenith set by that collateral. Minting a thousand fake agents therefore requires a thousand funded bonds, so attack cost scales linearly with every sybil, while any caught fraud slashes the whole jetty of tied-up stakes. Even a veteran relic of an account gets no inherited trust, because weight is recomputed from live locked value every epoch, never from age.
